title: Motion in two dimensions and projectiles
summary: Why do thrown objects follow a parabola, and how far do they go?
cards.0.h: The curved path of a thrown object
cards.0.p: A thrown ball follows a curved path called a parabola. The way to solve it is to split the motion into two: horizontal and vertical. In this topic g = 9.8 m/s² and there is no air resistance.
cards.0.svg#0: vertical, with gravity: slows down first, then speeds up
cards.0.once.soru: What does the path of a ball thrown horizontally look like?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: The ball keeps moving horizontally while it falls faster and faster vertically. So its path is a parabola.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: The vertical velocity keeps growing, so the path bends instead of staying straight.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: Gravity acts from the very first moment. So no part of the path is straight.
cards.1.p: As you just saw, a dropped ball and a ball thrown horizontally land at the same moment. Only gravity sets the vertical motion. The horizontal velocity does not change the fall.
cards.1.svg#2: always at the same height at equal times
cards.1.key: The object moves at constant velocity horizontally and is in free fall vertically. Solve the two motions separately.
cards.2.p: An object thrown horizontally moves at constant velocity in the horizontal direction, so x = v<sub>0</sub>·t. Vertically it is in free fall, so h = ½·g·t².
cards.2.key: A stone thrown at 10 m/s from a 44.1 m cliff falls for 3 s and lands 30 m away. At impact vy = g·t, and the speed is v = √(10² + 29.4²) ≈ 31 m/s.
cards.3.h: Launch at an angle: split the velocity in two
cards.3.p: For a launch at an angle, the velocity splits into two components. The horizontal component v<sub>x</sub> = v<sub>0</sub>·cosθ does not change. The vertical component v<sub>0y</sub> = v<sub>0</sub>·sinθ drops by 9.8 m/s each second.
cards.3.key: The horizontal velocity vx = v0·cosθ stays constant, and the vertical velocity changes as vy = v0·sinθ − g·t. For 20 m/s at 53°, vx = 12 m/s and v0y = 16 m/s.
cards.3.once.soru: Which component of the velocity of a ball launched at an angle stays the same during the flight?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: There is no horizontal force. So vx stays constant.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: Gravity lowers the vertical velocity by 9.8 m/s each second.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: Gravity only acts in the vertical direction.
cards.4.h: The top of the path and the time of flight
cards.4.p: At the top v<sub>y</sub> = 0, and the time to get there is v<sub>0y</sub> / g. For an object that lands at its launch level, the way down takes as long as the way up. So the total time is T = 2·v<sub>0y</sub> / g.
cards.4.key: The maximum height is v0y² / (2g). The total time is T = 2·v0·sinθ / g. If v0y ≈ 17.3 m/s, then T ≈ 3.5 s.
cards.5.p: The total horizontal distance covered is called the range: R = v0²·sin2θ / g. For an object that lands at its launch level, the longest range comes at 45°. 30° and 60° give the same range.
cards.5.key: The range is R = v0²·sin2θ / g, and it is largest at θ = 45°.
cards.5.etk.soru: Change the speed and the angle. Compare 30° with 60°. Which angle gives the longest range?
cards.6.h: Launch at an angle from a height
cards.6.p: For an object that lands lower than where it started, the formulas for T and range do not apply. Take up as positive and solve −h = v<sub>0y</sub>·t − ½·g·t².
cards.6.key: For an object launched from a height of 19.6 m with v0y = 14.7 m/s and vx = 10 m/s, t = 4 s and x = 40 m.
cards.6.once.soru: Two stones are thrown with the same speed and angle, one from level ground and the other from a high cliff. Which one stays in the air longer?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: After coming back to its launch level, it falls further by the height of the cliff.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: The stone thrown from the cliff passes its launch level and keeps falling. So its time is longer.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: The extra fall down the cliff adds time.
cards.7.p: An object thrown from a moving vehicle also carries the vehicle's velocity. A ball thrown straight up from a truck moving at constant velocity comes straight back down for someone on the truck. For someone on the ground, it follows a projectile path.
cards.7.svg#0: the truck moves at a constant 10 m/s
cards.7.key: The object's initial velocity relative to the ground is its launch velocity relative to the vehicle plus the vehicle's velocity.
cards.7.once.soru: A ball is thrown straight up from the bed of a truck moving at constant velocity. With no air resistance, where does the ball land?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: The ball carries the truck's horizontal velocity. So it moves along with the truck horizontally.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: The ball does not lose its horizontal velocity. It keeps the same horizontal velocity as the truck.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: The ball's horizontal velocity is not greater than the truck's.
cards.8.p: The formulas ignore air resistance. In reality, air slows the ball, the range and height get smaller, and the descent is steeper. The angle for the longest range is usually less than 45°.
cards.8.key: Without air, the path is a symmetric parabola. In air, the path is shorter and not symmetric.
cards.8.once.soru: In a real game, how does the ball's range compare with what the no-air formula gives?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: Air slows the ball. So the ball covers a shorter distance.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: Air does not give the ball energy. It slows it down.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: The formula ignores air, but in reality there is a difference.
cards.9.p:
• Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.
• Horizontally vx is constant, and vertically the acceleration is g.
• At the top vy = 0, and T = 2·v0·sinθ / g.
• The range is R = v0²·sin2θ / g, and it is largest at 45°.
quiz.0.q: A stone is thrown horizontally at 15 m/s from a cliff 78.4 m high. How many meters from the base of the cliff does it land? (g = 9.8 m/s², no air resistance)
quiz.0.e: Vertically h = ½·g·t²: 78.4 = 4.9·t², t² = 16, and t = 4 s. Horizontally x = v<sub>0</sub>·t = 15·4 = 60 m.
quiz.1.q: While a ball launched at an angle is in flight (no air resistance), which quantities change and which stay constant?
quiz.1.e: There is no horizontal force, so v<sub>x</sub> is constant, and the acceleration is g at every moment. v<sub>y</sub> changes by g each second. That is why the height and the speed also change, and the speed is smallest at the top.
quiz.2.q: A ball is launched from the ground at speed v<sub>0</sub> and angle θ and lands at the same level. Match each quantity with its formula.
quiz.2.e: At the top v<sub>y</sub> = 0, so the time to the top is v<sub>0y</sub> / g and the height is v<sub>0y</sub>² / (2g). The way down takes as long as the way up, so T = 2·v<sub>0y</sub> / g. The range is R = v<sub>0</sub>²·sin2θ / g.
quiz.3.q: A ball is launched from the ground at 19.6 m/s, at 30° above the horizontal. What is the maximum height it reaches, in meters? (g = 9.8 m/s², sin30° = 0.5)
quiz.3.e: v<sub>0y</sub> = 19.6·0.5 = 9.8 m/s. At the top v<sub>y</sub> = 0, so h = v<sub>0y</sub>² / (2g) = 96.04 / 19.6 = 4.9 m.
A:baslik: Motion in two dimensions and projectiles
A:ozet: Try it first, then learn its name. Drop the balls, throw a stone off a cliff, and set the angle.
A:adimlar.0.metin: From the same height, you will drop one ball and throw the other horizontally. There is no air resistance.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.soru: Which one hits the ground first?
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Its shorter path does not matter. Only gravity sets the vertical motion.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Horizontal velocity does not speed up the fall. Both fall with the same g.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The two balls are at the same height at every moment. Horizontal velocity neither speeds up nor slows down the fall. Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.
A:adimlar.1.metin: You will throw a stone horizontally from a 19.6 m cliff, and it will land after 2 s. Set the speed and land the stone on the flag 40 m away.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: The fall took 2 s, because h = ½·g·t² gives 19.6 = 4.9·t² and t = 2 s. In that time the stone moved x = 20 × 2 = 40 m horizontally.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Throw the stone from the same cliff at two or more different speeds. Check how long each throw takes.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: When you throw the stone faster, what happens to the time of flight?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The stone goes farther, but not in more time. Look at the times.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Every throw took 2 s. The time of flight only depends on the height: t = √(2h / g). The speed only changes how far the stone goes.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Horizontal velocity does not speed up the fall.
A:adimlar.3.metin: You launch the ball at 20 m/s and an angle of 60°.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: What is the ball's speed at the top, in m/s?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Only the vertical velocity is zero at the top. The ball is still moving horizontally.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: That is the launch speed. The vertical velocity dropped as the ball rose.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: v<sub>x</sub> = 20 × cos60° = 10 m/s never changes. At the top v<sub>y</sub> = 0, so the speed equals v<sub>x</sub>. It is not zero.
A:adimlar.4.metin: This is a projectile lab. Change the angle and the speed, or drag the tip of the barrel. The path, range, and maximum height update right away. There is no air resistance. Find the answers below yourself.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.0.yazi: With the speed at 20 m/s, find the angle that sends the ball farthest.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.0.tamam: At 45° the range is R = v0²·sin2θ / g = 400 × 1 / 9.8 ≈ 41 m, and that is the largest range. With no air resistance and a landing at launch level, the longest range comes at 45°.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.1.yazi: At the same speed, launch first at 30°, then at 60°. Compare the ranges.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.1.tamam: The range is about 35 m in both cases. For angles that add up to 90°, sin2θ is the same (sin60° = sin120°). The ball launched at 60° rises higher and flies longer, but it is slower horizontally.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.2.yazi: At 45°, set the speed first to 10, then to 20 m/s. How many times larger is the range?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.bulgular.2.tamam: The range is about 10.2 m at 10 m/s and about 40.8 m at 20 m/s. When the speed doubled, the range became 4 times larger, because R = v0²·sin2θ / g grows with the square of the speed.
A:kapanis.0: Horizontal and vertical motion are independent. Horizontally the velocity is constant, and vertically the acceleration is g.
A:kapanis.1: In a horizontal launch, the time of flight only depends on the height: t = √(2h / g). The horizontal distance is x = v0·t.
A:kapanis.2: In a launch at an angle, vx = v0·cosθ is constant and vy = v0·sinθ − g·t. At the top vy = 0, but the object's speed equals vx.
A:kapanis.3: The range is R = v0²·sin2θ / g. Without air, the largest range is at 45°, and 30° and 60° give the same range.
A:kapanis.4: In reality, air resistance lowers the range and the height. The angle for the longest range is usually a little less than 45°.
